key_insight: Domain-specific biomedical embeddings, especially BioBERT, improved detection of dosing-error risk in clinical trial protocols.
clinical_relevance: This could help flag higher-risk protocols earlier, supporting trial safety review and more informed monitoring decisions.
method: Encoded clinical trial text with transformer models: ClinicalBERT, PubMedBERT, BioBERT, and MedCPT.
Combined text embeddings with categorical metadata.
Tested classical ML and neural models, including logistic regression, gradient boosting, SVC, and residual neural networks.
evidence_signal: Using ROC-AUC for evaluation, BioBERT reached 0.794 with logistic regression, and the strongest models scored 0.821 to 0.853.
watch_item: Results come from experimental modeling on protocol text, so real-world deployment would need external validation and careful review of false alarms.
paper_title: CaresAI at CT-DEB26: Detecting Dosing Errors In Clinical Trials Using Domain-Specific Transformer Embeddings and Classification Models
